questions.q: What is the primary factor that determines when Kharif crops are sown?
questions.a: Kharif crops are sown at the beginning of the monsoon (June-July). A wrong answer suggests the student is confusing these with Rabi crops, which are sown after the monsoon in autumn.

questions.q: If a farmer needs a crop that requires a lot of water and warm weather, which season should they choose?
questions.a: They should choose the Kharif season. Choosing Rabi reveals a misunderstanding of the seasonal climate; Rabi crops grow in cooler, post-monsoon conditions.

questions.q: A farmer in Haryana harvests wheat in the spring. Based on this, when was the wheat likely sown?
questions.a: It was sown in autumn (October-November). If a student says June, they have failed to identify the sequential nature of cropping seasons.

questions.q: Compare the water needs of Kharif crops versus Rabi crops.
questions.a: Kharif crops require high water levels provided by the monsoon, whereas Rabi crops rely on moisture left in the soil or winter irrigation. Confusing these two shows a failure to link biological needs with seasonal climate.

questions.q: Why is it impossible to grow all crops at any time of the year in India?
questions.a: Crops have specific temperature and water requirements that only match certain seasons. A student failing this sees farming as a factory process rather than a system dependent on nature.

questions.q: Design a simple "Crop Calendar" for your region: list three crops and the season they belong to.
questions.a: The answer must correctly pair: Rice/Maize/Cotton with Kharif, and Wheat/Mustard/Barley with Rabi. An incorrect answer shows a lack of practical knowledge about local food sources.
